content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-physics-average-speed","title":"Average Speed","quick":"Average speed is total distance divided by total time taken. It tells how fast something moved on average, not the speed at every moment.","full":"Think of a bus going from home to the market, 120 km in 2 hours. It may go fast on open road and slow in traffic, but average speed just looks at the whole trip: total distance (120 km) divided by total time (2 h) = 60 km/h. This is the overall rate, not the speed shown at every instant on a speedometer.","traps":["Forgetting to convert hours and minutes into the same unit before dividing","Dividing time by distance instead of distance by time","Giving answer without unit (km/h)"],"misconception":"Child thinks average speed means the speed the car showed most often, not total distance over total time.","parent_questions":[{"q":"If the bus covers 90 km in 3 hours, what is its average speed?","expected_answer_hint":"30 km/h, found by 90 divided by 3"},{"q":"Why is average speed not the same as the speed shown on speedometer at one moment?","expected_answer_hint":"Because speed changes during the trip; average speed looks at the whole journey, not one instant"}],"check_question":{"q":"A scooter travels 150 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed?","options":["50 km/h","450 km/h","3 km/h"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct! 150 divided by 3 = 50 km/h.","wrong_feedback":"Divide total distance by total time: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 km/h."},"illustration":{"scene_prompt":"A small bus driving on a road from a house towards a busy market with fruit stalls.","labels":[{"text":"120 km","position":"top"},{"text":"2 hours","position":"bottom"},{"text":"60 km/h","position":"center"}]}}
